content.rendered:
Last week, I wrote about Bruce’s sublime “Fade Away.” It takes a lot of guts to cover it–there’s not much room (if any) for improvement.

But if anyone can do it justice, it’s Southside Johnny. His voice and style are perfectly suited for it, and he hits it out of the park. Just a beautiful, beautiful cover, from his 1997 Spittin Fire live album.

© May 3, 2018

excerpt.rendered: Southside Johnny turns in a gorgeously soulful, acoustic cover of “Fade Away.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Not Fade Away
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce covered "Not Fade Away" as far back as 1971 and as recently as last summer. It's always at the ready for an impromptu team-up--watch some of best ones inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Cover Me, Southside Johnny: All the Way Home
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: If you only know "All the Way Home" from the Devils & Dust album, then you don't know its original arrangement and best performance.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Walking Through Midnight
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One of the more under-the-radar Southside Johnny/Bruce Springsteen collaborations, "Walking Through Midnight" closed Southside's first solo album in 1988.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fade Away
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From his Destination Anywhere tour in 1997, Jon Bon Jovi treats Japanese fans to a faithful cover of Bruce Springsteen’s “Fade Away.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jambalaya (On the Bayou)
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: At an impromptu soundcheck-turned-preshow, Bruce, Southside, and friends play a loose, fun cover of a Hank Williams classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Little Girl So Fine
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Now here's a recipe: Start with inspiration from Leiber and Staller, add lyrics by Bruce, music by Steve, and lead vocals by Southside Johnny. Ice with backing vocals by The Drifters, and you've got pure pop confection.
